body.x: Softgenomics Corp. (CEO Kwang Hee Lee) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Softgenomics is a group of experts in bioinformatics, genomics, and field molecular diagnostics technology, specializing in diagnostics and solutions for remote infection diagnostics, skin microbiome related products, and services.

The products for skin microbiome testing presented in the exhibition consist of a kit, equipment, and a web service system that reports the analysis results. Users can get reports on individual skin microbiomes and useful information, along with custom cosmetic solutions on-site in a matter of hours. Softgenomics finds its differentiator in interpreting skin biologically instead of skin type through existing questionnaires or images.

Just as intestinal microbiomes are deeply related to health, many microbes that live in the skin also play important roles in skin health. Softgenomics CEO Kwang Hee Lee said that, “At present, NGS-based microbiome analysis is costly and time-consuming, making it inefficient for personal skin care. We developed the product that inspects microorganisms easily and quickly on the site to accurately diagnose skin and recommend ingredients that are conducive to the health of each individual.”

The products for skin microbiome testing were pilot produced in November, 2022 for market testing with researchers and partners around the world, and partner agreements are now underway for production next year. The licensing process is also in progress, leading to the launch in the global market, and sales in the domestic and overseas markets are planned for the first half of 2023.

CEO Lee explained the company's involvement in the event, saying, "By participating in this CES, we will unveil our new microbe-based on-site skin diagnostics products, identifying and collaborating with global buyers and investors.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
